newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche confident of timely Euro start.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche confident of timely Euro start.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG management board member Rolf Breuer said Germany's largest commercial bank was convinced the single European currency will be launched on schedule in January 1999.

In an interview with Swiss magazine Finanz und Wirtschaft, Breuer said strong political will would ensure a timely start for the Euro with at least six European Union states and possibly as many as eight.
"Deutsche Bank is firmly expecting the introduction of European currency union at the planned time," Breuer said in the interview, which will be published on Wednesday.

"As well as France and Germany, the Benelux countries and Austria will take part as well as Denmark and Ireland -- conditions permitting," he said in the interview. A copy was made available in advance of publication.
"Our preparations are running at top speed," Breuer said of efforts at Deutsche to prepare for the new currency.
Breuer also said he was confident the planned currency, to be called the Euro, would be as stable as Germany's much-revered mark.

"I think the market has already answered that. Interest rates have converged... That shows that the market expects stability. The old European anchor currency was the mark, the new one will be the Euro," Breuer said.
On the strength of the Euro, he noted that several currencies -- the Dutch guilder, the Austrian Schilling and the French franc -- had been closely tied to the mark for the past few years.

"We are practically living in European Economic and Monetary Union already. It is just that nobody has called it that yet and that there has always been a way out, at least theoretically," Breuer said.
